Use case: stylized-concept. Create one original square nature cutout for Glaze, Lensleaf Glade. The first thing someone sees at small size is one familiar whole five-lobed autumn maple leaf, facing forward on a slight clockwise tilt, with complete sharp lobe tips, a coherent copper-orange perimeter and a complete slender curved stem. The complete leaf and stem fit inside the central 76 percent of the image. True transparent alpha outside the whole leaf. The leaf is flat in the image, with a restrained amber edge and clear silhouette.

Inside the leaf, lay a coarse two-row, three-column register of six broad, flat, touching optical views. They all show the same tiny woodland scene in the same light and the same warm colors: ONE highly simplified pale ivory mushroom with a single broad cap and thick stalk, a spruce-green far vertical tree trunk, and one broad moss slope. No other miniature objects. Leave the edge of the leaf uninterrupted where it clips the outer windows. Keep the six views adjacent with very thin or invisible seams. Use a strong value difference between the ivory mushroom and the dark trunk so they can both be seen in a tiny preview. Give each window the same warm amber earth and dark natural evergreen. The near mushroom shifts progressively to the right relative to the far trunk as you look from left to center to right within each row. It partly overlaps the trunk in the center. The near mushroom sits slightly lower relative to the distant trunk in the second row. Preserve one clear cap in every full view. The relative positions, rather than differences in colors, let the viewer see six different directions on the same scene. This is invented artistic integral imaging, without actual capture or reconstruction.

Keep the outer maple shape visibly uninterrupted and strong even at 85 px. Broad bold forms and restrained tonal detail, with two or three secondary shade transitions per window. No tile bevels, glass beads, shiny lens surfaces, metal leading, dark grid border, bright cut-paper seams, unrelated samples, checkerboard colors, photographic leaf veins sprawling over the little views, labels, text, logo, watermark, noise overlay, haze, outline glow or exterior shadows. No rectangular background, stand, frame, room or device. One square pure piece of original art with a completely transparent exterior. No external source images.

The whole natural subject, with a visible repeated near and far view, reads at 85 px.

Keep all parts of the main subject within the central 76 percent of the square, with large transparent side margins and every natural projection intact. Allow small or narrow parts to carry plain solid amber and spruce if needed for their shape. All exterior is true transparent alpha. Use case: stylized-concept. Create one original opaque portrait phone wallpaper for Glaze Lensleaf Glade, with a canvas aspect ratio close to 1290 by 2796. The one input is our own maple leaf artwork. Use its warm illustrated color fields, complete copper maple leaf and broad flat viewpoints of one mushroom glade as the established visual language. Make one quiet and recognizable autumn woodland around it. The large areas use flat refined shading, with deep spruce, warm moss, and copper and pale cream accents. The surrounding woods behind the subjects are uninterrupted and dim, with a few tall spruce silhouettes and a soft moss floor. Give the viewer a natural arrangement on a single woodland floor.

Across the middle of the scene, one bent maple branch leads from a whole bright copper leaf with its full curved stem to a wren perched on its attached short twig. The whole maple leaf shows the same few warm windows as the reference. The cream cap moves from one side of the dark trunk through overlap to the other side. A whole comma butterfly, small enough to feel at home in the canopy, hovers nearby with four scalloped orange wings. Below them a whole resting russet fox faces inward, with both ears, pointed muzzle, paws and curled full tail visible. A single small whole acorn rests on the moss near the fox, with cap, nut and full short stem. Give the wren, butterfly, fox flank and acorn two to four broad flat contiguous views of the same cream mushroom glade. The near cream cap shifts against the dark far trunk. Keep the foliage and shapes distinct and the alternate views sparse, with only a few large bold motifs. The woodland itself is one continuous scene in the same colors, with open dark space around the main shapes. Preserve useful breathing room between heads, limbs, stems, butterfly wings and the margins.

Compose the whole group within the central 72 to 76 percent of the image width. The animals, leaf, butterfly and acorn occupy roughly 50 to 55 percent of the height, centered around 57 percent down the frame. Leave the upper 24 percent quiet dark spruce for a phone clock. Leave roughly 12 percent to either side and the bottom 13 percent quiet, even on a shorter phone crop. No bright branch ends or animals touching the border. Keep the mood warm and grounded with clear natural shapes and no glass or glitter. No real lens capture, data or optical reconstruction. No unrelated miniatures, grid of unrelated pictures, isolated sticker backgrounds, lighting streaks, banners, interface, text, names, numbers, logos or watermark. No external images.

ownerSteering: Whole recognizable autumn plants and wildlife. Artwork corners leave breathing room on deep spruce. A small maple outline and one vein suit compact live headers. The wallpaper gives the maple the strongest woodland views and sets the other subjects naturally into the glade.

conceptReferences.scope: Read the authors' Stanford report abstract on the microlens array and computationally accessible viewpoints. The planned fiction is neither a real raw microimage nor capture data.
Read the authors' description of subimages and extraction of perspective views. Use the generic visual idea of separate viewpoints only. No source images or calibration are used.
Read indexed excerpts of the primary Optica paper on integral imaging and elemental images. No optical design or figure is used.

conceptReferenceScope: Researchers' descriptions of adjacent samples and different viewpoints inspired the repeated broad views in the artworks. These are original fictional images.
